outcome: No change since 26 January 2024: the five remaining Seventeen or Bust/PrimeGrid candidates (k = 21181, 22699, 24737, 55459, 67607) remain untested to completion, with no new prime found and no elimination since 10223 in October 2016; the conjecture that 78,557 is the smallest Sierpiński number is still open.
summary: Selfridge's conjecture (that 78,557 is the smallest Sierpiński number) remains open with no change since the frozen revision. The search is carried out by PrimeGrid's Seventeen or Bust subproject, which since the last elimination (k=10223, prime found 31 October 2016, per the PrimeGrid forum thread id=1647) has had exactly five remaining candidates: k = 21181, 22699, 24737, 55459, 67607. PrimeGrid's live statistics page (stats_sob_llr.php, fetched 2026-09-22) still lists exactly these five k values as in-progress, with hundreds of thousands of candidate n values still to be tested (e.g. 88,147 candidates for k=21181, 418 workunits in progress for k=55459) and no new primes reported. The current (2026-09-12-dated) revision of Wikipedia's own 'Sierpiński number' and 'Seventeen or Bust' articles still list the same five candidates with no update describing an elimination or resolution. A PrimeGrid 'SoB Telephone Challenge' ran 7-17 March 2026, confirming the subproject is still actively crunching workunits, but no result from it (or any other period since January 2024) eliminated a candidate or otherwise advanced the conjecture. No AI system was found to be involved in any capacity — this is a pure distributed-computing (BOINC/LLR primality-testing) search, not a domain where AI-generated proofs, bounds, or search strategies were reported. I found no papers, preprints, blog posts, or announcements suggesting any AI involvement in the Sierpinski problem specifically. This matches the triage's 'none' verdict and I did not find anything it missed.
competing_reading: None. There is no plausible alternate classification here — every source, from the PrimeGrid live stats page to the current Wikipedia articles, agrees the same five candidates remain untested to completion and no elimination or proof has occurred since 2016, well before the window.
what_would_settle_it: A PrimeGrid announcement (forum post or stats page update) of a new prime found for one of k = 21181, 22699, 24737, 55459, or 67607 (which would yield partial/progress by eliminating a candidate), or a proof/disproof of the conjecture itself (which would yield resolved/claimed). Absent either, the status stays open.
